title: Igusa varieties, compactified period fibers and torsion concentration, Part II: compact unitary Shimura varieties
summary: The compact endgame of Caraiani–Scholze: for compact unitary Shimura varieties of Kottwitz's simple type and of quasi-split type with F⁺ ≠ ℚ, attach Galois representations to systems of Hecke eigenvalues in mod-ℓ cohomology and prove that, when the residual representation is decomposed generic at a suitable auxiliary prime split in the imaginary quadratic field, the localized cohomology is concentrated in the middle degree. It combines the parent's Igusa geometry and perversity with the trace formula comparison showing that generic Igusa cohomology lives only on the μ-ordinary stratum.
readme:
**Purpose.** This roadmap is Part II of Igusa varieties, compactified period fibers and torsion concentration (IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration) and starts where that roadmap stops. The parent builds the Igusa varieties, the fibres of the Hodge–Tate period map, the perversity of nearby cycles and the minimal-stratum concentration for compact PEL data of type (A)/(C), and assembles the non-compact theorem of Caraiani–Scholze for the quasi-split U(n,n) datum. This Part II proves the compact theorem of Caraiani and Scholze, On the generic part of the cohomology of compact unitary Shimura varieties (Ann. of Math. 186 (2017)): Theorem 5.5.7, §5.6, Theorem 6.3.1 and Theorem 1.1.

**Scope.** Compact unitary PEL data of type (A) over F = F⁺·𝒦: Kottwitz's simple Shimura varieties (Case 1) and data quasi-split at finite places with F⁺ ≠ ℚ (Case 2), of any rank n and any signature; auxiliary primes split in 𝒦, not necessarily totally split in F.

**Conventions.** Sets S_i are defined with ι_p^{−1}∘τ; Hecke polynomials use geometric Frobenius as in AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII AG2.0; Newton classes lie in B(G, μ^{−1}) with the covariant slope normalization of the parent; Red^b includes the modulus twist of PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17/E74; localization is always at the contraction of 𝔪 to the Hecke operators away from the auxiliary prime.

**Layers.** IG.8 data, Hecke algebras and duality; IG.9 the μ-ordinary obstruction for Case 2; IG.10 Kottwitz's simple Shimura varieties; IG.11 torsion concentration and the end theorems.

**Boundaries.** The Igusa geometry, compact fibre theorem, perversity and Lemma 6.2.2 are the parent's (IG.1, IG.3, IG.4, IG.5); Shin's trace formula, base-change transfers, the stable–twisted identity and Newton reduction are EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison's; Galois representations of conjugate self-dual automorphic representations and decomposed genericity are AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII's; B(G), J_b and Lemma 5.5.8 are BunGAndNewtonStrata's; the perfectoid Shimura variety and π_HT are PerfectoidShimuraVarieties'. The ordinary Igusa formal schemes of Siegel varieties (Boxer–Pilloni) are a separate direction, proposed as their own roadmap.

**Sources.** Caraiani–Scholze (Annals 2017, journal pages); Shin's appendix to Goldring (Compositio 2014) for base change.

**Recorded gap.** Base change for the division-algebra groups of Case 1 (the cited appendix covers B = F only).

stages.title: Compact unitary PEL data, Hecke algebras and duality
stages.description:
## IG.8. Compact unitary PEL data, Hecke algebras and duality

Fix F = F⁺·𝒦 with 𝒦 imaginary quadratic and a compact unitary PEL datum of type (A) of one of two kinds: Case 1, B a central division algebra of degree n over F with an involution of the second kind and V ≅ B (Kottwitz's simple Shimura varieties); Case 2, B = F, F⁺ ≠ ℚ, G quasi-split at every finite place and every prime ramified in F in Spl_{F/F⁺}. Record the signatures (p_τ, q_τ), the dimension d = Σ_{τ∈Φ} p_τq_τ = ⟨2ρ, μ⟩, the set S, the level K = K_SK^S and the moduli problem S_K (|ker¹(ℚ, G)| copies of the Shimura variety). Prove that at p ∉ S with K_p hyperspecial the integral model is smooth and proper (Case 1 by PELModuli's properness for division End_B(V); Case 2 because anisotropy leaves no cusp labels).

At a prime p ∉ S split in 𝒦, p = uu^c, construct the primes 𝔭_i of F above u, the sets S_i = {τ | ι_p^{−1}∘τ induces 𝔭_i} (CS17 prints ι_p∘τ), the decomposition G_{ℚ_p} ≅ ∏_i Res_{F_{𝔭_i}/ℚ_p}GL_n × 𝔾_m, the product decomposition of B(G, μ^{−1}) and of J_b, and the Shapiro identification of a factor with a single nontrivial τ with B(GL_n/F_{𝔭_i}, μ_{i,τ}^{−1}), including the central twist p^{c_i} that the source omits.

Define 𝕋^S = ⊗′_{q ∈ Spl_{𝒦/ℚ} ∖ (S ∪ {ℓ})} ℤ[G(ℚ_q)//K_q], the operators T_{i,v} (with the similitude factor ℤ_q^×) and the Hecke polynomial P_v(X) = Σ_i (−1)^i q_v^{i(i−1)/2}T_{i,v}X^{n−i}. Prove ι(T_{i,v}) = T_{n,v}^{−1}T_{n−i,v} for the involution [KgK] ↦ [Kg^{−1}K], the roots q_v^{n−1}λ^{−1} modulo 𝔪^∨, ρ_{𝔪^∨} ≅ ρ_𝔪^∨ ⊗ ε̄^{1−n} and the invariance of decomposed genericity. Prove Hecke-equivariant Poincaré duality on S_K (with local-system coefficients) and on Mantovan's Igusa varieties, with the dual ideal. Define CS-auxiliary pairs (p, 𝔭) for a residual representation and prove their existence in the two situations of CS17 Remarks 6.3.2–6.3.3 (Remark 6.3.3 as corrected).

Acceptance: d = 2 for n = 3 with signatures (1,2), (0,3); 𝔪^∨ for roots {1, 2} at q_v = 7 over 𝔽_11 has roots {7, 9}; a Case 2 datum indefinite at every infinite place with n ≥ 3 is not compact.

stages.title: Generic principal series and the μ-ordinary obstruction for the quasi-split datum
stages.description:
## IG.9. Generic principal series and the μ-ordinary obstruction (Case 2)

**Dependencies:** IG.8.

For the Case 2 datum, at a prime p ∉ S split in 𝒦 with K_p hyperspecial, prove the stable Igusa trace identity tr(φ | ι_ℓ[H_c(I^b_Mant, ℚ̄_ℓ)]) = |ker¹(ℚ, G)|τ(G) Σ_n⃗ ε_n⃗ I^{𝒢_n⃗θ}_spec(f^n⃗θ) for acceptable φ_p (CS17 Theorem 5.3.2), from Shin's stable Igusa trace formula for PEL type (A) and the stable–twisted identity of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison, both available for every rank n and every archimedean signature.

Prove that the normalized Newton reduction Red^b_n⃗ kills π^n⃗_p as soon as one factor transfers to a generic principal series of GL_n(F_{𝔭_i}) and J_{b_i} is a non-quasi-split inner form (CS17 Lemma 5.4.3). Prove the spectral expansion of the Igusa trace for arbitrary φ_p and the occurrence of eigensystems in BC^{S′}([H_c]^{S′-ur}) with the corrected hypothesis on total contributions (CS17 Lemma 5.5.1 and Corollary 5.5.2, corrected E77, E79). Construct the r-part of the base-changed Igusa class. Prove that a non-μ-ordinary class has a non-quasi-split factor at a nontrivial 𝔭_i when each S_i has at most one nontrivial embedding (via Lemma 5.5.8 of BunGAndNewtonStrata BG1), and conclude Theorem 5.5.7: under that condition and a decomposition of r at the nontrivial 𝔭_i into characters with non-cyclotomic ratios, the r-part vanishes for every non-μ-ordinary b.

Acceptance: for [F⁺:ℚ] = 2, n = 2, signature (1,1) at one embedding of the CM type and (2,0) at the other, and p totally split, the basic class does not contribute to a generic r; the proper datum (n/2, n/2) carries the coefficient 1/2.

stages.title: Kottwitz's simple Shimura varieties
stages.description:
## IG.10. Kottwitz's simple Shimura varieties (Case 1)

**Dependencies:** IG.8, IG.9 (the Newton reduction lemma and the lemma on non-μ-ordinary classes).

For the Case 1 datum with B split above p, prove that only the stable term survives in Shin's Igusa trace formula (CS17 Proposition 5.6.1): every proper elliptic endoscopic datum G_{n₁,n₂} has a place where the local index of B does not divide n₁, where the transfer vanishes. Prove the stable Lefschetz identity Red^b_n([H(Sh, ℚ̄_ℓ)]) = ε_G d(G_ℝ)[H_c(I^b_Mant, ℚ̄_ℓ)] from Arthur's L²-Lefschetz formula for the compact quotient, the stabilization with no proper endoscopy, Lemma 5.4.2 and the extension to all φ_p, and deduce the Igusa cohomology formula of Corollary 5.6.2 through Matsushima's formula, with an explicit coefficient c(π_f).

State the Galois representations r_{π,ℓ} of cohomological automorphic representations of G attached through base change (attributed by CS17 to Shin's appendix to Goldring 2014, which treats only B = F: recorded gap and request to AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII AG2.2). Construct the r-part of the Igusa class and prove Corollary 5.6.3, the analogue of Theorem 5.5.7.

Acceptance: for n = 1 there is no endoscopy and the identities reduce to class field theory for the torus; for b basic the reduction is the Jacquet–Langlands map of the global cohomology.

stages.title: Torsion concentration for compact unitary Shimura varieties
stages.description:
## IG.11. Torsion concentration for compact unitary Shimura varieties

**Dependencies:** IG.8–IG.10; the parent's IG.3 (compact fibre theorem) and IG.4 (compact minimal-stratum concentration); IG.5 (Lemma 6.2.2).

Prove the contraction lemma for localizing at 𝔪 ∩ 𝕋^{S∪{p}}, the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence H^a_cts(K_p, H^b(𝒮_{K^p}, 𝔽_ℓ)) ⇒ H^{a+b}(S_K, 𝔽_ℓ) with its two localized consequences (the nonvanishing statement in the corrected form E96), and the Leray reduction of the localized cohomology of the perfectoid Shimura variety to the cohomology of the Igusa varieties Ig^b through π_HT. At a Newton class b of minimal d_b with nonzero localized Igusa cohomology prove concentration in degree d_b at finite level, integrality, the passage to compact supports with the dual ideal, and the existence of a contributing eigensystem lifting 𝔪^∨ (Deligne–Serre).

Conclude CS17 Theorem 6.3.1: (1) for every 𝔪 in the support of H^*(S_K, 𝔽_ℓ) a unique semisimple ρ_𝔪 with char ρ_𝔪(Frob_v) = P_v mod 𝔪 at the places above Spl_{𝒦/ℚ} ∖ (S ∪ {ℓ}) (two auxiliary primes, E97); (2) if ρ_𝔪 admits a CS-auxiliary pair then H^j(S_K, 𝔽_ℓ)_𝔪 ≠ 0 only for j = dim S_K. Deduce Theorem 1.1 (complete decomposition at p, or one decomposed-generic place in the definite-but-one case) and the integral and twisted-coefficient forms of Remarks 1.3 and 1.7.1.

Acceptance: H^0(S_K, 𝔽_ℓ) ≠ 0 shows that localization is necessary; for d = 0 the theorem says the localized cohomology lives in degree 0.
